description:
FOUND s492a (Opus, 2026-09-20) as #1919's second half; #1919 itself (the
ADJACENT-occurrence loss, `"$v$v"` printing one `$v`) is FIXED in that
member, and this is the residue it did NOT reach: a different mechanism.
PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00 and unchanged by the #1919 fix (probed on
both).

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3;
scratch/s492a/probes/m6-braced.pl in the s492a worktree):
  { my $v = 1; print "inner $v\n"; }   # an inner-block decl: gives the
                                        # rename a region
  my $v = 7;
  sub f { print "C[${v}$v]\n"; }        # a sub reading the file-level one
  f();
  perl: inner 1 / C[77]
  PCL:  Transpile failed: Parser2 TODO: file lexical 'v' captured by sub f
        (the WHOLE FILE, not one statement)

`"$v$v"` in the same shape works after #1919; `"${v}${v}"` and
`"${dir}${file}"` refuse the same way.  So `_interp_fixer` DOES carry a
braced arm (`\$\{\s*NAME\s*\}`) and can rewrite the text -- what refuses is
upstream of it: the CAPTURE CHECK that decides whether the sub may be
renamed at all does not count a braced interpolation as a reference it can
rewrite, so it declines and the file is refused.

WHY IT MATTERS: `"${prefix}_suffix"` is everyday Perl -- the braced form is
exactly what you write when the name is followed by word characters.  The
refusal needs BOTH an inner-block redeclaration of the name AND a sub
capturing the file-level one, which is why no corpus file has met it.

STANDING RULES THAT APPLY (project memory): "a SIGIL- or SCOPE-blind capture
refusal is a BUG -- delete/rename, never narrow", and "interpolation scanning
happens in Pl/InterpScan.pm or not at all".  So the fix is to route the
capture question through InterpScan's variable EVENTS -- which already know
the braced, array, element and hash-element spellings -- rather than to add
another regex beside `_interp_fixer`'s.

BAR: a Pl/ name-resolution change => THE FULL SWEEP IS THE GATE (#296),
corpus-diff, emission A/B, gate-SET scan over BOTH populations (a refusal
stops firing), `--quick` companion once; guard rows in
Pl/t/interp-rename-sections-01.t beside #1919's, inverse-verified.
subject: A BRACED interpolation `"${v}"` of a renamed file lexical refuses the WHOLE FILE -- "Parser2 TODO: file lexical 'v' captured by sub f" -- where the unbraced `"$v"` is renamed fine
